title: Capital Gain Discount changes 1 July 2027
body:
O.P.
Here to go again... Labor can't leave this alone. Hopefully it's Dead On Arrival but the unions are pushing for change and well we all what happens...
https://www.news.com.au/nati onal/politics/jim-chalmers-t argets-tax-break-that-superc harged-boomer-wealth/news-st ory/70cc0ef805b2b3be6192bf84cb534bea

---- replies ----
[User #18356030340 postspgdownloadWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
j??01 writes...
Here to go again... Labour can't leave this alone.
At least one party is trying to be fiscally responsible. All governments tax and I'm not sure why anyone believes one tax is more or less sacrosanct than another tax? No one doubts that CGT discounts are a big contributor to sky high housing prices.
Any sensible policy might allow significant tax breaks for the first (PPOR) and second (IP) houses that you own but why should there be such a generous tax break beyond that?
Lets wait and see what they propose anyway. If its anything like the tweaks to super tax I suspect it will be pretty mild an only actually affect less than 5% of the wealthier citizens. (As the article mentions, the wealthiest fifth of Australians accrue 90 per cent of the benefits of CGT discounts)
[User #595340433 postsOzraForum Regular] pgdownload writes...
Any sensible policy might allow significant tax breaks for the first (PPOR) and second (IP) houses that you own but why should there be such a generous tax break beyond that?
This.
Tabloid media is making a fuss over nothing, it will likely be grandfathered in or an exemption of 1x IP per person/cap up to x amount or pretty generous tiered system.
It is now or nothing if we are ever going to legislate or take action on property investing/policy.
[User #2215925380 postscanon1dNeed more pixelsWhirlpool Forums Addict] j??01 writes...
Labor can't leave this alone.
Change is needed to make residential property investment less attractive, as part of other changes to ensure housing is affordable. There are plenty of investment alternatives to residential housing.
We don't know what is planned. The changes might be small, might include grandfathering existing properties, might only be available to a set number of properties and so on.
Right wing media will try and blow up any proposal, but change is needed. Let's wait and see what surfaces.
[User #34704512232 postsj??01Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
canon1d writes...
Change is needed to make residential property investment less attractive, as part of other changes to ensure housing is affordable. There are plenty of investment alternatives to residential housing.
While I agree, making housing more affordable takes more than just reducing CGT.
It needs a multi-pronged approach like reducing migration, scrap or reduce negative gearing, build more houses Australian want to buy and not just apartments.
It'll take a very brave government to implement any of these.
Right wing media will try and blow up any proposal, but change is needed. Let's wait and see what surfaces.
It doesn't matter whether it's Right Wing or Left Wing media, housing affordability requires more action then just reducing CGT.
[User #14774613670 postsJacketedCognitive dissonance much?Whirlpool Forums Addict] j??01 writes...
, housing affordability requires more action then just reducing CGT.
Granted.. what else does it require?
What other levers are you talking about?
[User #277686443 postsBabyJesusForum Regular] Good start to meaningful reform.
CGT discount on non-productive asset speculation makes no sense except serve the interests of the asset holders, it has no meaningful benefit to the economy.
[User #2599603453 postsTommiMWhirlpool Forums Addict] Ozra writes...
Tabloid media is making a fuss over nothing, it will likely be grandfathered in or an exemption of 1x IP per person/cap up to x amount or pretty generous tiered system.
This would be nice. I'm in a situation where I owner occupied, but due to changes in work, I now rent out the house to a long term tenant who is very unlikely to want to buy or move (and probably not at market rate), and I have not decided the next step for it yet but that is some time away.
[User #4896531354 postsMega-MegatronWhirlpool Enthusiast] pgdownload writes...
No one doubts that CGT discounts are a big contributor to sky high housing prices.
Are we sure of this? Do we have any data to support it?
Lots of people (read investor developers) are already using Company structures to retain more profits and CGT discounts do not apply in a company structure. If the CGT discount is gone, what stops others from using company structures?
Moreover, I dont believe the CGT discount can be canned completely.. It can be overhauled with a new calculation method though.
If they are targetting, non-company held properties, then the better way would be to look at the negative gearing instead of CGT discount. Negative gearing is a bigger reason lots of people buy investment properties IMO.
[User #905923215 postsyovpaForum Regular] Albo & Jimbo must be fairly confident the opposition cannot get their act together before 2028.
[User #2133121125 postsTheronWhirlpool Forums Addict] yovpa writes...
Albo & Jimbo must be fairly confident the opposition cannot get their act together before 2028.
Given what is happening I would be astonished if they could.
[User #115471405 postsDemanufactureTime Destroys EverythingWhirlpool Enthusiast] Mega-Megatron writes...
If they are targetting, non-company held properties, then the better way would be to look at the negative gearing instead of CGT discount. Negative gearing is a bigger reason lots of people buy investment properties IMO.
Both Negative Gearing and CGT are covered in a lot of the submissions to the senate committee – for CGT – https://www.aph.gov.au/Parlia mentary_Business/Committees/ Senate/Operation_of_the_Capi tal_Gains_Tax_Discount/Capit alGainsTaxDiscount/Submissions
[User #2858703278 postscurtlyDo donuts make you fat?Whirlpool Forums Addict] It's possible that they will just move back to the old indexing methods. With modern computers it would be pretty easy to work out.
As I and others have said before (on other threads) – if you don't sell you never pay CGT so taking away the discount will only encourage people to hold onto their real estate.
[User #4637864638 postsmegadriveWhirlpool Forums Addict] curtly writes...
As I and others have said before (on other threads) – if you don't sell you never pay CGT so taking away the discount will only encourage people to hold onto their real estate.
Discourages short term flippers which is what we want, market is flooded with people selling the same property in identical condition ½ years later
[User #8983113658 postsIkerukuchiWhirlpool Forums Addict] curtly writes...
It's possible that they will just move back to the old indexing methods. With modern computers it would be pretty easy to work out.
To be fair for a property it was pretty easy to work out back then as well (and 30 years before that for that matter)
The other thing that people need to remember is that once you’ve held a property for 12-15 years or so the indexing method means less tax than the discount method so the classic strategy of negative gearing a property through your higher income earning years and then moving it on after retirement when you’ve got much lower income and the gains can be split between a couple is even more incentivised.
While I’m on the side of increasing wealth taxes and reducing income taxes I think we need to move cautiously and Chalmers makes me nervous as he tends to only want to change little bits rather than looking holistically so I’m worried we’ll make it worse.
[User #18356030340 postspgdownloadWhirlpool Forums Addict] Mega-Megatron writes...
Are we sure of this? Do we have any data to support it?
Probably oodles. When it comes to house prices its pretty well established that any discount generally just feeds into higher asking prices down the line. You only have to look at first home buyer grants to understand that.
Demanufacture writes...
Both Negative Gearing
I believe they've ruled out touching Negative Gearing at all this election cycle. Probably enough to start with CGT.
Mega-Megatron writes...
Lots of people (read investor developers) are already using companys If the CGT discount is gone, what stops others from using company structures?
Depends on how comprehensive the law changes are. If nothing else it places "investor developers" in a separate basket to "mum and dad" investors where the rules can be tweaked without affecting everyone.
j??01 writes...
making housing more affordable takes more than just reducing CGT.
Frankly the "affordable housing" boat has sailed. Housing prices are now completely disconnected from their utilitarian value. Rich people use them as a place to store wealth. Like a coveted Ming vase its value is now only who can pay the most for it.
Reducing the CGT discount to my mind is more about moving to sensibly tax wealth. You're right that there's a lot of areas that need reform – land tax, sales tax, CGT, stamp duty, GST, red tape, approval delays, etc. Labour are suggesting a few big things are on the table and its watch this space for now...
